summary.text: A 56-year-old man with previously confirmed situs inversus totalis was admitted to a thoracic surgery department in January 2014 for a 2.5 cm right lung tumor of unknown etiology detected on chest X-ray. He had no clinical symptoms. Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed situs inversus and showed a 28 × 22 mm tumor in the sixth right segment with a 9 mm satellite tumor and enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes.

FDG-PET/CT and endobronchial ultrasound were inaccessible. Ultrasound fine needle aspiration of the lung tumor was ineffective and cancer cells were not observed in the supraclavicular lymph node biopsy specimen, although the high CEA level of 95.3 ng/mL suggested adenocarcinoma in stage N2. Bronchofiberoscopy showed right-sided bronchial anatomy typical of the left lung and left-sided anatomy corresponding to the right lung.

He qualified for surgery via right thoracotomy. Intraoperatively, left-lung anatomy was found on the right side with an undeveloped posterior interlobar fissure and nodal metastases in groups 5 and 7, and the procedure was limited to sixth segmentectomy with mediastinal and lung hilar lymphadenectomy. The final diagnosis was adenocarcinoma G2 with a partial micropapillary G3 component, T1bN2Mx/IIIA. The postoperative course was uneventful. He received adjuvant chemo- and radiotherapy and died after 12 months due to metastatic brain spread.
